title: non_iid: gate the bitstring estimators on the sample width, not the observed alphabet (§3.1.3)
body:
Fixes #253.

## What

Gate the bitstring estimators in `cpp/non_iid_main.cpp` on the **sample width** (`data.word_size > 1` / `== 1`) instead of the **observed alphabet size** (`data.alph_size > 2` / `== 2`). One file, 18 lines, each a one-token change of the same condition; no estimator, cutoff, rounding or numeric path is touched.

## Why

SP 800-90B §3.1.3: "If the sequential dataset is not binary … L samples (each having n bits) is considered as a bitstring of size nL … H_I = min(H_original, n × H_bitstring, H_submitter)". Binary-ness is a property of the sample width n. The code tested the number of distinct observed values, so an n-bit dataset in which exactly two values occur was relabelled to {0,1} and assessed as a 1-bit source — no bitstring formed, the n × H_bitstring term dropped, and an explicitly declared width ignored. Details and the measured effect are in #253.

## Reproduction (before → after)

```
python3 -c "import random;r=random.Random(12345);b=[r.randrange(2) for _ in range(1000000)];open('twoval.bin','wb').write(bytes(2*x for x in b))"
./ea_non_iid -vv twoval.bin      # before: Assessed 0.92162256445118362 (no Bitstring lines)
                                 # after:  H_bitstring Per Symbol = 0.17960299911578648, Assessed 0.17960299911578648
./ea_non_iid -vv twoval.bin 8    # before: Assessed 0.92162256445118362 (declared width ignored)
                                 # after:  H_bitstring Per Symbol = 0.31779050350127225, Assessed 0.31779050350127225
```

## What does not change

Width-1 datasets and datasets with more than two values satisfy both conditions identically, so:

- `cpp/selftest/selftest` against `refdata` is unchanged for every `bin/` sample (max deltas 1e-15..4e-10, the same platform deltas as before the change on this build — macOS, Apple clang + libomp).
- A 1,000,000-sample 16-valued 4-bit control reports exactly the same figure before and after (3.7390649510685936).
- `data.alph_size <= 1` (constant data refusal) is left as is, and every estimator call still receives `alph_size`.
